researcher_notes: Atimonan One Energy (Meralco PowerGen unit) proposed an LNG import terminal with FSU as part of converting its shelved Atimonan coal plant to a 2,400-MW gas CCGT after the 2020 coal moratorium. The gas/LNG conversion was formally reported in 2023 (DENR/EIA submission and public scoping April 2023; BusinessWorld 2 Aug 2023). One solid mainstream source verified; April-2023 corroborations (Manila Standard 'Atimonan switches to 2,400-MW LNG plant'; Bilyonaryo 17 Apr 2023) describe the same proposal but returned HTTP 202 to the verifier, so single-source / non-primary -> medium.

Batangas Clean Energy, Inc. (Lucio Tan group / Blackstone-backed Gen X) first publicly surfaced the LNG-terminal-plus-CCGT project in 2019 (BusinessMirror, 23 Dec 2019, reported BCE had 'applied for NTP already'); DOE certified it as an Energy Project of National Significance on 30 Oct 2020. Year of first proposal = 2019, but the only verifiable anchor is the 2020 EPNS certification (Manila Times, 9 Nov 2020, contains '2020' + 'Batangas Clean Energy'); the Dec-2019 first-proposal article failed the verifier (HTTP 403). Partial/indirect support for the 2019 milestone -> low.

This is a PLANNED (projected) retirement of the interim offshore FSRU arrangement (FSRU BW Batangas, a 5-year time-charter that began with the vessel's June 2023 arrival, ops from late 2023/2024). No source states a specific year for the interim FSRU's retirement/replacement; the planned end is a forward-looking inference (~end of the 5-year charter). No citable year -> UNRESOLVED.

First Gen's permanent Batangas LNG import terminal (FGEN LNG) has well-documented later milestones - Tokyo Gas joint-development agreement 5 Dec 2018, DOE notice-to-proceed effective 7 Mar 2019, groundbreaking 28 May 2019 - but First Gen's original public proposal of an LNG terminal at the Batangas Clean Energy Complex predates these and could not be pinned to a single citable first-proposed year in this pass. Earliest firm milestone is the Dec-2018 Tokyo Gas JDA; the true 'proposed' (order 1) year is earlier and unverified -> UNRESOLVED.

The shelving of Shell's revived Tabangao FSRU (Pilipinas Shell, Batangas) is an inference from inactivity ('inferred 2 y'), not a formally announced event. After June-2022 plans (PHP3.5B investment, construction to begin 2024) the project quietly did not proceed; no source states a specific shelved/paused/suspended year for this post-2021-revival phase. No citable year -> UNRESOLVED. (Note: an earlier, distinct 2018 drop is documented but corresponds to an earlier timeline entry, not this order-5 one.)

Energas was formed in 2017 as a buyers' consortium (Younus Brothers Group, Sapphire Group, Halmore Power) to set up Pakistan's first private merchant LNG terminal (FSRU) at Port Qasim. Two independent 2017 publishers verified: The Nation (17 Sep 2017, plan for a private terminal completing 'early 2019') and Dawn (2017, 'YB Group, Sapphire to set up LNG terminal at Port Qasim'). Proposal year = 2017.

This is a PLANNED (projected) FID, not an actual one. Energas obtained an OGRA construction licence (~2020-2021) and said it was 'all set to start construction' (Arab News, 2021), but the project stalled and never reached a confirmed Final Investment Decision; no source gives a specific FID year. No citable FID year -> UNRESOLVED.

Engro Elengy Terminal (EETL) and Excelerate Energy publicly proposed expanding/replacing the existing FSRU Exquisite with a larger newbuild FSRU via a heads-of-agreement announced 30 Jan 2020. Two independent origins verified: Offshore Energy (independent media) and Excelerate Energy (sponsor press release). Proposal/announcement year = 2020. (Project later stalled and was presumed shelved ~2023, but the order-1 'proposed' milestone is 2020.)

Pakistan GasPort (PGPC) and Trafigura announced their commitment to proceed with a SECOND LNG terminal/merchant FSRU at Port Qasim at the inauguration of the first terminal (BW Integrity) on 20 Nov 2017. The operator group's own site (ag.com.pk, primary) explicitly states the 2017 second-terminal commitment (verified 2017 + 'Trafigura' + 'second'). Offshore Energy's Nov-2017 inauguration piece is a supporting reference but Trafigura was also a stakeholder in the first terminal, so it does not by itself isolate the second-terminal proposal -> kept as 1 strong/primary source = medium.

T10 is one of the three GL1K Skikda trains that SURVIVED the 19 Jan 2004 explosion (which destroyed units 20/30/40, demolition contract Jan 2007). The old surviving trains were decommissioned when the new single GL1K 'Rebuild' mega-train (4.5 Mtpa) replaced the complex; that replacement train was commissioned/inaugurated 25 Jan 2014 (Algerie360, French). IGU's 2016 World LNG Report records Skikda old trains decommissioned in 2014 (available only via GEM-derived summaries, not independently citable). Year 2014 is the best-supported decommissioning year; the cited French source documents the 2014 replacement-train commissioning (proxy for old-train retirement), not an explicit per-train shutdown statement -> low/partial.
